title: Photosynthesis and Respiration
summary: How green plants make food from carbon dioxide and water using light energy, and how all living things release energy from food by respiration.

notes.text: Green plants are **producers**: they make their own food. In the leaves, the green pigment **chlorophyll** (found in **chloroplasts**) traps energy from sunlight. The plant uses this energy to turn **carbon dioxide** from the air and **water** from the soil into **glucose** (a sugar). **Oxygen** is given off as a by-product.

notes.caption: In photosynthesis a leaf uses sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose, and gives off oxygen.
What photosynthesis needs and where it comes from
rows: Enters through tiny pores called **stomata** on the underside of the leaf
Absorbed by root hairs and carried up the stem in **xylem** vessels
Absorbed by chlorophyll in the chloroplasts
Found in chloroplasts, mostly in leaf cells

items: Used immediately in **respiration** to release energy for growth and repair.
Changed into **starch** and stored in leaves, roots (carrots, sweet potatoes), stems (potatoes) and seeds.
Changed into **cellulose** to build cell walls.
Combined with nutrients from the soil to make proteins and oils.

notes.title: Testing a leaf for starch
notes.problem: How can you show that a leaf has made starch by photosynthesis?
steps: Boil the leaf in water for about a minute to kill it and soften the cells.
Place it in warm ethanol (in a water bath, never over a flame) to remove the chlorophyll; the leaf turns pale.
Rinse the leaf in water to soften it.
Add a few drops of **iodine solution**. A blue-black colour shows that starch is present; brown-orange means no starch.
notes.answer: Iodine turns blue-black where starch is present.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: To prove that light is needed, keep a plant in the dark for two days (to use up its starch) and then cover part of one leaf with foil before putting it in the light. Only the uncovered part tests positive for starch.

**Cellular respiration** happens in the **mitochondria** of every living cell, in plants and animals, day and night. Glucose reacts with oxygen to release **energy**, which the organism uses to move, grow, keep warm and repair itself.
Respiration that uses oxygen. It releases a large amount of energy.
Respiration without oxygen. Yeast makes alcohol and carbon dioxide (fermentation); hard-working muscles make lactic acid, which causes cramps.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: Plants do NOT only photosynthesise while animals respire. Plants respire all the time too. In bright light, photosynthesis is faster than respiration, so a plant gives off more oxygen than it uses.

notes.title: Comparing the two processes
notes.problem: Compare the word equations for photosynthesis and respiration. What do you notice?
steps: Photosynthesis: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (needs light energy).
Respiration: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water (releases energy).
The substances that go in to one process are what come out of the other.
notes.answer: They are opposite processes: photosynthesis stores energy and respiration releases it.

items: It is the start of almost every food chain: all food energy comes from the sun through plants.
It replaces the oxygen in the air that living things use up.
It removes carbon dioxide from the air, helping to slow global warming.

questions.prompt: Name the green pigment that traps light energy in leaves.
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is found in the chloroplasts.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide enters through the stomata.

questions.prompt: What are the products of photosynthesis?

questions.prompt: Give TWO differences between photosynthesis and respiration.
questions.memo:
Any two, 2 marks each (both sides of the difference):
✓✓ Photosynthesis uses CO₂ and water; respiration uses glucose and oxygen
✓✓ Photosynthesis happens only in light; respiration happens all the time
✓✓ Photosynthesis takes place in chloroplasts; respiration in mitochondria
✓✓ Photosynthesis stores energy; respiration releases energy

questions.prompt: Explain why photosynthesis is important for animals, even though animals do not photosynthesise.
questions.memo:
✓ Plants are the start of food chains, so animals get their food energy from plants (directly or indirectly) (1)
✓ Photosynthesis releases the oxygen animals need for respiration (1)
